vasco_f_2: [cold, controlled anger] I know what you were doing in his office. You were looking for something to prove that someone was doing something wrong.
vasco_v_12: [contemptuous] Your word's under a hotel, Rayco.
vasco_v_14: [trembling, trying to joke] I'm sorry. I've been working on a Saturday. [pause] I know You're busy.
vasco_m_seventh_2: [urgent] When the light leaves the shaft, the door's open. [pause] Flat, Alan. Onto the great triangle.
vasco_m_twenty: [horrified] Look. Up the shaft, at a slant. [pause] He's sending the sun back. Without him the moon's no one's. And the sea's no one's.
vasco_f_van_2: [exasperated] I signed the transfer sheets myself. They're in the conservation lab in the museum's basement. You could have asked me. [pause] You could have just asked me.
vasco_p_6: [warm, moved] Thank you. For coming. For the beach and the jacket and all of it. I know this isn't your world.
vasco_m_excuses_1: [hurt, quiet] [pause] I know I left. I know about the rum. [pause] That's not the bit that hurts.
vasco_m_knew_3: [voice breaking] I told myself it couldn't be you. There are a great many Portuguese men in Las Palmas. I lay in that vault all night and told myself that, over and over.
vasco_m_knew_5: [tearful, tender] Then you came down the steps into the water to get me. And I thought: if he tells me, he'll tell me before I ask. And if he doesn't, he'll wait until I do.
vasco_m_twice: [out of breath, raw, close to tears] I've let go of people before. I got on a train once, in the middle of the night, and let go of the best man I ever knew.
alan_f_told_all_2: [rushed, breathless] The tide a step higher every morning. My family's mark on a bell in Santa Ana. A sealed letter. I faxed it to Inês.
alan_stay_3: [flustered, defensive] I'm just talking. I'm just... I just needed somewhere to sit. I'm not...
alan_s_go: [bitter, self-loathing] I could go now, before he turns round. Money on the table, out of the door, someone else by lunchtime. [pause] I always have.
alan_s_window_1: [ashamed, quiet] I lied to him. He asked me, straight out, and I lied.
alan_s_sketch_2: [realising, alarmed] Baute. [pause] One a month, one by one, down into a vault under the mountain. Only he has the key. And Vasco signed the transfer sheets himself.
alan_s_sketch_4: [bitter, ashamed] I heard every word of it last night. I was too busy watching Rafa's hands to listen.
alan_m_1d: [quiet, haunted] When it came, it took him. It took half the people on the shore. It had me too, and it let me go, because of whose blood I've got. [pause] [grim] I don't think it'll do that twice.
alan_m_so_this: [whispering, letting go] So this is how she went. Alone in the water, when the door shut.
alan_m_today: [steeling himself] Tell him. Today. Not when it's convenient.
alan_m_plain: [quiet, plain] I broke both of them. Both your rules. I didn't tell you first. And I did it on purpose.
alan_m_plain_3: [ashamed] And then I lied to him about you. And I would have lied to you about him. On Saturday morning I was already working out how.
alan_m_blame_2: [distraught, self-pitying] I'm the worst thing that's ever happened to you. Worse than the Church. Worse than Rome.
alan_s_father: [distant, sad] I don't know why I'm thinking of my father. Pedro Sanches. He went out fishing off Cascais when I was a boy, and never came back. [pause] [grief] I can't remember his face any more.
alan_w_dawn_say: [quiet, frightened] Say it. I did see a ghost. The thing from the cistern. It's here, and I'm frightened.
alan_su_told: [quiet, haunted] Because I've stood in it. [pause] A cistern under Lisbon. Black water, and something in the dark that knew me. And Doña Pino's list has my name at the bottom.
alan_th_desk_2: [excited, urgent] 'Twenty-fourth, mediodía.' Noon. [pause] It's him. I don't know how it connects to a fisherman drowned in his bed. But it connects. It has to.
alan_w_coffee: [tender, amused] [pause] He was right. It's terrible.
alan_th_wake: [guilty, quiet] He came in at midnight and left at six. Between those, he slept like a man with a clear conscience. I lay there with mine.
alan_s_vasco: [dread, realising] Whoever understands the lock. [pause] And Vasco's up there, understanding it. He's the best in the world at understanding things.
alan_s_radio_lie: [low, angry] He's lying. Vasco's up there, and Baute's lying about where.
alan_call_sat_3: [worried] I can't reach him. He's on the mountain. The radio's off.
alan_su_idiot_4: [desperate] I've been doing everything on my own because I'm frightened of needing anyone. Two people have drowned in their beds, and Vasco is up on that mountain with Rayco Baute, and I can't reach him.
